questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Congress enacted a statute that annually awards federal funds to states that must be used to improve the quality of public education. Every state agreed to participate in this federal program. On average, the funds awarded by the federal program comprise 15% of a state's overall annual budget.
Several years later, Congress enacted another statute that expanded this federal program to reduce the academic achievement gap between high-performing and low-performing public schools. A provision of this federal statute requires states to administer a statewide academic test to students that is then used to assess the academic performance of public schools. States that choose not to comply with this testing requirement will no longer receive any federal funding from the program and may suffer budgetary shortfalls as a result.
A state that has chosen not to comply with the testing requirement has sued the federal government, arguing that the statute's provision is unconstitutional.
Which of the following is the state's best argument?

choices.A: Incentivizing states to adopt federal policies exceeds the scope of Congress's spending power.
choices.B: The condition placed on the receipt of federal funding is unduly coercive.
choices.C: The funding of public education has traditionally been performed by the states.
choices.D: The Tenth Amendment grants states immunity from direct federal regulation.

questions.explanation:
Conditional federal funding
(Article I, section 8 spending clause)

Conditions must meet all the following criteria:

  • clearly stated & unambiguous
  • reasonably related to federal interest in funded program
  • do not require states to engage in unconstitutional activity
  • do not unduly coerce states into accepting

The taxing and spending clause gives Congress broad discretion to spend for the general welfare, such as improving the quality of public education. Congress can use this spending power to incentivize states to adopt federal policies by placing appropriate conditions on the receipt of federal funds (Choice A). A condition is appropriate when it:

  • is clear and unambiguous (eg, requiring states to comply with the testing requirement or lose federal funding)
  • is reasonably related to the purpose for which the funds will be expended (eg, requiring academic testing to reduce the academic achievement gap)
  • does not require recipients to engage in unconstitutional activity (eg, developing and administering a statewide academic test is not unconstitutional) and
  • is not unduly coercive.

A condition is unduly coercive if it amounts to a "gun to the head" of a state. Although SCOTUS has not provided concrete guidance on how to make this determination, it has invalidated a condition that would have withheld 10% of a state's overall budget.*

Here, the condition on the receipt of federal funding would withhold 15% of an average state's annual budget. This amounts to a "gun to the head" and is unduly coercive since states that do not comply with this condition may suffer significant budgetary shortfalls. Therefore, this is the state's best argument that the provision is unconstitutional.

*In contrast, SCOTUS has upheld a condition that withheld less than 1% of a state's overall budget.

(Choice C) Although the funding of public education has traditionally been performed by the states, the spending clause gives Congress the power to spend for the general welfare—including public education.

(Choice D) The Tenth Amendment grants states immunity from federal regulations that compel or unduly coerce them to enact state laws or enforce federal laws. However, states must comply with other types of direct federal regulation (eg, EPA pollution standards).

📌 Educational Objective

Congress may use its spending power to regulate states by placing conditions on the receipt of federal funds that (1) are clear and unambiguous, (2) are reasonably related to the purpose for which the funds will be expended, (3) do not require recipients to engage in unconstitutional activity, and (4) are not unduly coercive.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. I, § 8, cl. 1 (taxing and spending clause).
  • South Dakota v. Dole, 483 U.S. 203, 212 (1987) (holding that Congress can place a condition on the receipt of federal highway funding that amounts to less than 1% of a state's overall budget).
  • Nat'l Fed'n of Indep. Bus. v. Sebelius, 567 U.S. 519, 581–82 (2012) (explaining that Congress cannot place a condition on the receipt of Medicaid funds that amounts to 10% of a state's overall spending).
questions.zh-question:
国会颁布了一项法规，每年向各州提供联邦资金，这些资金必须用于提高公共教育的质量。每个州都同意参与这个联邦项目。平均而言，该联邦项目提供的资金占一个州年度总预算的15%。

几年后，国会又颁布了一项法规，扩大了该联邦项目，旨在缩小高表现和低表现公立学校之间的学业成就差距。该联邦法规的一项条款要求各州对学生进行全州范围的学业测试，该测试随后用于评估公立学校的学业表现。选择不遵守此项测试要求的州将不再从该项目中获得任何联邦资金，并可能因此遭受预算短缺。

该条款是否可能合宪？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为附加在接受联邦资金上的条件具有过度胁迫性。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为第十修正案授予各州免受联邦直接管制的豁免权。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为国会有权为公共福祉支出。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为第六条的至上条款要求各州执行联邦法律。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Federal-State Relations - Taxation And Spending

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会利用联邦拨款诱导州采纳政策时，如果以撤销占州预算总额比例过高的资金为威胁，将构成过度强迫，违反第十修正案。

三秒认题路径：

联邦拨款附条件 → 违约撤资比例巨大（占州预算15%） → 剥夺州选择权 → 构成过度强迫（Undue Coercion） → 违宪

核心法律规则

国会可通过 征税与支出权（Taxing and Spending Clause） 向各州拨付有条件资金，以诱导各州采纳联邦政策。但此类拨款条件必须符合以下四项标准：

  • 条件明晰无歧义： 州必须明确知晓不配合的法律后果；
  • 关联性： 条件必须与所资助项目的联邦利益合理相关；
  • 不诱导违宪： 条件不得强迫或诱导各州从事违宪行为；
  • 非过度强迫（Not Unduly Coercive）： 资金撤回力度不能大到实际上强迫州执行（不得构成“指着脑袋的枪” gun to the head）。
核心判例： NFIB v. Sebelius (2012) —— 美国最高法院首次判定，国会以撤回占州总预算约 10% 的全部 Medicaid 联邦资助来逼迫各州扩大医保，属于过度强迫（unduly coercive），因侵犯州主权而违宪。本题中扣除占州总预算 15% 的资金力度更大，同样构成违宪强迫。

思维导图

1. 明晰告知 (Clear Condition)
州如果不遵守学术测试要求，就失去联邦教育资金。后果明确无歧义。
2. 目的相关 (Reasonably Related)
测试用以评估表现、缩小成绩差距。与“提高教育质量”合理相关。
3. 不诱导违宪 (Not Unconstitutional)
要求州组织测试本身不侵犯任何个人宪法权利，亦不违法。
4. 非强迫性 (Not Coercive) ❌ 拦截
威胁扣除占州总预算 15% 的联邦资金，已剥夺州自主选择权，构成“强迫违宪”。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：第十修正案保护州免受联邦直接指挥，国会不可以直接立法强迫州办事，所以此条款应以“直接监管”或侵犯州传统领域（教育）为由认定违宪。

但考试真正问的是：国会并未直接以行政命令强迫，而是通过“不配合就不给钱”进行利诱。只有当利诱金额过大（本题高达15%的整体预算），导致州完全没有实际选择余地时，利诱才在法理上等同于强迫（coercion）。

司法考试看的是「手段上是否实质剥夺了州的自主权」，而不是「国会能不能资助传统州务」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干中扣除占州总预算 15% 的资金额度极大，实质剥夺了州的选择权，属于 unduly coercive 强迫违宪。

❌ 概念混淆 | 权力边界误判

✕ A: 看到 incentivize 就选错——国会利用拨款引导地方政策本身完全合法，并不超权。

❌ 法律适用 | 传统领域豁免误判

✕ C: 误将 traditionally performed 当成绝对屏障，国会只要出于公共福利即可对传统领域拨款。

❌ 事实误判 | 监管形式性质偷换

✕ D: 漏看本题是“利诱”而非“直接命令”，第十修正案的 direct federal regulation 豁免在此不适用。

这题建议用什么方法？

识别资金占比：看到拨款条件争议，立刻看扣款占州总预算的比例（通常以10%为分水岭判定是否过度强迫）。

考场速记

附条件拨款五部曲考点速记：

国会拨款附条件，必须通过五关卡：1. 公共福利；2. 明确告知；3. 目的相关；4. 不诱导违宪；5. 不能过度强迫。

记忆重点：扣款占州总预算比例（如本题的 15% 或 NFIB 案中的 10%）过高，即是“指着脑袋的枪”，属于强迫违宪！

reason.en: Frames the legal question regarding the limits of Congressional power.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state imposes a tax on the "income" of each of its residents. As defined in the taxing statute, "income" includes the fair rental value of the use of any automobile provided by the taxpayer's employer for the taxpayer's personal use.
The federal government supplies automobiles to some of its employees who are residents in the state so that they may perform their jobs properly. A federal government employee supplied with an automobile for this purpose may also use it for the employee's own personal business.
Assume there is no federal legislation on this subject.
May the state collect this tax on the fair rental value of the personal use of the automobiles furnished by the federal government to these employees?

choices.A: No, because such a tax would be a tax on the United States.
choices.B: No, because such a tax would be a tax upon activities performed on behalf of the United States, since the automobiles are primarily used by these federal employees in the discharge of their official duties.
choices.C: Yes, because an exemption from such state taxes for federal employees would be a denial to others of the equal protection of the laws.
choices.D: Yes, because the tax is imposed on the employees rather than on the United States, and the tax does not discriminate against persons who are employed by the United States.

questions.explanation:
Federal immunity from state & local taxes/regulations
Tax/regulation Definition Permissibility
Direct Applies to federal government—including its agencies & instrumentalities Immune unless:
• Congress consents to tax/regulation
Indirect Applies to affiliates—including persons/entities employed by or doing business with federal government Not immune unless:
• Congress grants immunity or
• tax/regulation discriminates against or substantially interferes with federal duties

Under the Article VI supremacy clause, states are prohibited from taxing the federal government—including its agencies and instrumentalities—without congressional consent. But states can tax the federal government's affiliates—including federal employees (as seen here)—unless:

• Congress has granted the affiliate immunity

• the tax discriminates against the federal government or its affiliates or

• the tax substantially interferes with the affiliate's ability to accomplish its federal purpose or duties.

Here, the state seeks to collect an income tax on the value of the personal use of employer-provided automobiles from federal employees (not the U.S. government) (Choice A). Congress did not grant these employees immunity, and the tax is nondiscriminatory since it applies to automobiles provided by any employer. Additionally, the tax does not substantially interfere with the employees' federal duties since it only applies to their personal use of the automobiles. Therefore, the state may collect this tax from the federal employees.

(Choice B) Although the automobiles may primarily be used by these federal employees in the discharge of their official duties, the tax only applies to personal use of the automobiles. Therefore, it is not a tax upon activities performed on behalf of the United States.

(Choice C) Under the equal protection clause, state actions that do not substantially impact a fundamental right or intentionally discriminate against a protected class (as seen here) are subject to mere rational basis scrutiny. State action almost always satisfies this standard, so a tax exemption for federal employees would likely be sustained under this clause.

📌 Educational Objective

States can tax the affiliates of the federal government unless (1) Congress has granted the affiliate immunity, (2) the tax is discriminatory, or (3) the tax substantially interferes with the affiliate's federal purpose or duties.

📚 References
  • Graves v. New York, 306 U.S. 466, 486–87 (1939) (holding that a state income tax imposed on federal employees is not an unconstitutional burden).
questions.zh-question:
某州对其每位居民的“收入”征税。根据税法规定，“收入”包括纳税人因个人使用而由其雇主提供的任何汽车的公允租赁价值。

联邦政府为其在该州居住的部分雇员提供汽车，以便他们能正常履行工作职责。为此目的获得汽车的联邦政府雇员也可以将其用于个人事务。

假设没有关于此事的联邦立法。

该州是否可以就联邦政府提供给这些雇员的汽车的个人使用公允租赁价值征收此税？

zh-choices.A: 不可以，因为这种税收将构成对美国的征税。
zh-choices.B: 不可以，因为这种税收将构成对代表美国履行的活动征税，原因是这些汽车主要由联邦雇员在履行其公务时使用。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为豁免联邦雇员缴纳此类州税将构成对他人法律平等保护权的剥夺。
zh-choices.D: 可以，因为该税是向雇员而非向美国征收，且该税并未歧视受雇于美国的人员。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Federal-State Relations - Federal immunity

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：联邦免税权（Federal Immunity）仅直接保护联邦实体本身，州可以对联邦雇员的个人所得（包括雇主提供车辆的个人私用价值）征收普适且非歧视性的所得税。

三秒认题路径：

联邦提供车辆 → 雇员私用福利折税 → 纳税人是个人（非联邦） → 无国会免税立法且不具歧视 → 州征税合宪（选 D）

核心法律规则

根据宪法第六条的 最高条款（Supremacy Clause），各州在未经国会明示同意前，禁止直接对联邦政府及其派出机构与工具（Agencies and Instrumentalities）进行课税或监管。

但是，此免税权不保护与联邦交易或受雇于联邦的 关联方（Affiliates / Employees）。州可以对联邦雇员个人征收所得税，只要该税款满足以下“三无”合宪标准：

  • 无立法豁免： 国会未立法明确豁免该雇员的纳税义务；
  • 无歧视（No Discrimination）： 税收属于一般普适税，不针对联邦雇员进行差别对待；
  • 无实质干涉（No Substantial Interference）： 不严重干扰雇员执行联邦公务（如本题中仅就车辆的 personal use 个人私用部分征税）。
核心判例： McCulloch v. Maryland (1819) —— 确立了联邦实体免受州直接课税的宪法原则；但后续判例（如 Graves v. O'Keefe）明确限制其范围，判定对联邦雇员的薪金或福利课征普适性个人所得税并不违反联邦免税权。

思维导图

第一关：州税直接课征的对象是谁？
联邦政府/实体/财产:
❌ 直接课税 (Direct Tax) → 联邦绝对免税（除非国会同意） [排除 A]
联邦雇员 / 关联方个人:
第二关：国会是否明文立法给予其免税待遇？
是:
❌ 违宪（遵从联邦立法免税）
否:
第三关：州税是否构成歧视或实质性干涉联邦公务？
是 (歧视或干扰公务):
❌ 违宪 [排除 B]
否 (普适居民税，且仅限 personal use 个人用途):
✅ 合宪 (Valid State Tax) → 选 D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：联邦汽车属于联邦政府所有，州不能对联邦财产或其公务活动进行课税，因此此税必然违宪。

但考试真正问的是：该税究竟课征于谁？由于州税法的课税对象是雇员的「个人所得」（将私用车辆折算为收入），属于对雇员的间接税（Indirect Tax），且并未歧视或妨碍其执行联邦职务。

司法考试看的是「实际纳税主体是谁及是否妨碍公务」，而不是「该福利物品最初由谁提供」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

本税由联邦雇员个人承担，非直接课税于联邦，且对所有居民一视同仁无歧视，故州可以依法征收。

❌ 概念混淆 | 课税主体认定错误

✕ A: 错在把对雇员的间接课税当成对 United States 的直接课税。

❌ 事实误判 | 公私用途范围混淆

✕ B: 忽视了本税仅针对 personal use（个人使用），而非公务活动。

❌ 法律适用 | 平等保护原则误用

✕ C: 误用 equal protection，给联邦雇员免税本身并不会导致违宪。

这题建议用什么方法？

看清课税主体：区分直接税（对联邦）与间接税（对雇员），间接税只要无歧视、无干涉即合宪。

考场速记

联邦免税权（Federal Immunity）判定口诀：

“直接税联邦，绝对不可以；间接税个人，三无就合法。”

具体而言：如果税收是针对联邦实体（直接税），通常违宪；如果是针对联邦雇员/承包商个人（间接税），只要国会无免税立法、州税无歧视、对公务无实质干涉，即属合宪。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A county in State A is located adjacent to the border of State B. The communities located in the county are principally suburbs of a large city located in State B, and therefore there is a large volume of traffic between that city and the county. While most of that traffic is by private passenger automobiles, some of it is by taxicabs and other kinds of commercial vehicles.
A county ordinance provides that only taxicabs registered in the county may pick up or discharge passengers in the county. The stated purpose of this ordinance is to reduce traffic congestion. The ordinance also provides that only residents of the county may register taxicabs in that county.
Which of the following is the proper result in a suit brought by State B taxicab owners challenging the constitutionality of this county ordinance?

choices.A: Judgment for the county, because State B taxicab owners do not constitute a suspect or quasi-suspect class and the ordinance is reasonably related to the legitimate governmental purpose of reducing traffic congestion.
choices.B: Judgment for the county, because the ordinance forbids taxicabs registered in other counties of State A as well as in states other than State A to operate in the county and, therefore, it does not discriminate against interstate commerce.
choices.C: Judgment for the State B taxicab owners, because the fact that private passenger automobiles contribute more to the traffic congestion problem in the county than do taxicabs indicates that the ordinance is not a reasonable means by which to solve that problem.
choices.D: Judgment for the State B taxicab owners, because the ordinance unduly burdens interstate commerce by insulating the county taxicab owners from out-of-state competition without adequate justification.

questions.explanation:
Dormant commerce clause
(state regulation of interstate commerce)
Type of regulation Examples Standard
Discriminatory
(favors in-state interests)		 • Taxing out-of-state products more heavily
• Requiring use of in-state products/services 		Unconstitutional unless:
• furthers legitimate state interest and
• no reasonable alternative
Nondiscriminatory
(otherwise burdensome)		 • Prohibiting all commercial vehicles on state highways
• Overly strict requirements for all commercial shipments 		Unconstitutional if:
• burden clearly exceeds local benefits

The ability of state and local governments to regulate interstate commerce is limited by the dormant commerce clause. Under this clause, these entities are generally prohibited from discriminating against or otherwise unduly burdening interstate commerce. As a result, a state or local action that discriminates against interstate commerce—ie, an action that protects in-state over out-of-state economic interests—is invalid unless:

  • it furthers a legitimate, noneconomic state or local interest and
  • no reasonable alternative is available to achieve this interest.

Here, the State A county ordinance discriminates against interstate commerce since it only allows county residents to register and operate taxicabs in the county—thereby insulating them from out-of-state competition. The ordinance furthers the county's legitimate, noneconomic interest in reducing traffic congestion. But reasonable alternatives are available (eg, investing in public transportation). Therefore, the ordinance unduly burdens interstate commerce without adequate justification, and judgment for the State B taxicab owners is proper.

(Choice A) Taxicab owners are not a suspect or quasi-suspect class (ie, protected class), so the ordinance likely satisfies the Fourteenth Amendment equal protection clause under mere rational basis scrutiny. Nevertheless, the ordinance is invalid because it violates the dormant commerce clause.

(Choice B) The ordinance's unlawful discrimination against interstate commerce is not negated by the fact that it also discriminates against residents of other State A counties.

(Choice C) Although private passenger automobiles contribute more to traffic congestion in the county than taxicabs, the ordinance is a reasonable means to solve that problem since it alleviates some congestion. But it is still invalid because it discriminates against interstate commerce despite the availability of reasonable alternatives.

📌 Educational Objective

A state or local action that discriminates against interstate commerce violates the dormant commerce clause unless (1) it furthers a legitimate, noneconomic state or local interest and (2) no reasonable alternatives exist.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. I, § 8, cl. 3 (commerce clause).
  • Dean Milk Co. v. Madison, 340 U.S. 349, 354–55 (1951) (holding that a city's ban on the sale of milk processed outside city limits discriminates against interstate commerce and violates the dormant commerce clause).
  • 15A Am. Jur. 2d Commerce § 105 (2019) (explaining the proper standard of review for a law that discriminates against interstate commerce).

该县的一项法令规定，只有在该县注册的出租车才能在该县接送乘客。该法令的既定目的是为了减少交通拥堵。该法令还规定，只有该县的居民才能在该县注册出租车。

在B州出租车车主提起诉讼，质疑该县法令合宪性的案件中，以下哪项是正确的结果？

zh-choices.A: 判决该县胜诉，因为B州出租车车主不构成受质疑类别或准受质疑类别，且该法令与减少交通拥堵这一合法的政府目的有合理关联。
zh-choices.B: 判决该县胜诉，因为该法令禁止在A州其他县以及A州以外的其他州注册的出租车在该县运营，因此，它没有歧视州际贸易。
zh-choices.C: 判决B州出租车车主胜诉，因为私人乘用车对该县交通拥堵问题的贡献大于出租车，这一事实表明该法令并非解决该问题的合理手段。
zh-choices.D: 判决B州出租车车主胜诉，因为该法令在没有充分正当理由的情况下，使该县出租车车主免受州外竞争，从而过度地负担了州际贸易。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Federal-State Relations - The Dormant Commerce Clause

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：在休眠商业条款（Dormant Commerce Clause）下，地方性法规针对跨州商业的歧视（discrimination）及其严格审查标准的适用条件。

三秒认题路径：

外州车主受阻 → 仅限本地居民运营与注册 → 构成跨州商业歧视 → 启动严格审查 → 存在合理替代方案 → 判定违宪

核心法律规则

休眠商业条款的审查机制

依据休眠商业条款（Dormant Commerce Clause），限制州和地方政府规制跨州商业。审查分为两大路径：

  • 歧视性规章（Discriminatory Regulations）：如果法规在条文上或实质上优待本地人、排斥外州人（即地方经济保护主义），则被推定违宪。除非政府能证明同时满足：
    1. 规章是为了促进正当的、非经济性的地方利益（如缓解交通、环保等）；且
    2. 没有其他合理的无歧视性替代方案（no reasonable nondiscriminatory alternatives）。
  • 非歧视性规章（Nondiscriminatory Regulations）：法规对本地及外州人一视同仁但仍有附带限制，适用比照平衡测试（Pike balancing test）：除非其对跨州商业的负担明显超过本地带来的利益，否则合宪。
核心判例： Dean Milk Co. v. Madison — 即使地方规章不仅限制了外州人，也限制了本州内其他地区的人，只要其核心是给本地（本县）居民设定运营特权并阻碍了跨州商业，仍被判定为跨州商业歧视。

思维导图

第一关：法规是否构成“歧视”跨州商业 (Discriminatory against interstate commerce)？
【是 (YES)】 仅允许本地居民注册并运营出租车 ➔ 排斥了外州竞争。
第二关：是否能通过严格审查 (Strict Scrutiny) 的双重要求？
条件 1： 是否有正当的非经济地方利益？
✓ 满足：缓解交通拥堵（reduce traffic congestion）属于正当非经济性利益。
条件 2： 是否【无其他合理替代方案】 (No reasonable alternatives)？
✕ 失败：县政府完全可以通过限制总牌照数或加收高峰拥堵费等无歧视手段解决，无需彻底禁止外地车。
判定结果： 法规违宪，外州车主胜诉 (Judgment for State B owners) ➔ 锁定 D
【否 (NO)】 一视同仁但附带限制 ➔ 适用 Pike 平衡测试。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：该法令把本州内其他县的出租车和外州出租车一起禁了，既然本州其他县也受罚，这就不叫歧视外州吧？

但考试真正问的是：该法令是否通过构筑壁垒，将跨州商业竞争隔绝开来，以保护本地（本县）居民的经济利益？

司法考试看的是「法规是否构筑了地方保护主义壁垒」，即使它把本州其他县的人也一起挡在外面，只要它给本地（本县）居民设定了特权并排斥了跨州商业竞争，在休眠商业条款下它依然被认定为「歧视外州商业」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

该规章通过 only residents may register 排斥外地竞争，构成跨州商业歧视，且因存在合理替代方案而违宪。

❌ 概念混淆 | 审查标准张冠李戴

✕ A: 误套用平等保护的 suspect class 标准而漏看了商业条款限制。

❌ 法律适用 | 歧视豁免条件误判

✕ B: 误以为限制本州其他县就能洗白其对跨州商业的 discriminate 歧视。

❌ 事实误判 | 手段合理性偏离

✕ C: 纠结于私家车与出租车比例，试图以手段非 reasonable means 抗辩。

这题建议用什么方法？

优先看主体限制：一旦发现地方规章限制“非本地居民”运营注册，直接推定歧视，启动严格审查排除干扰项。

考场速记

休眠商业条款（DCC）做题两步走：

1. 看是否有歧视： 只要是对外排斥、对内优待（即使本州其他县也被排除），就构成 discrimination ➔ 推定违宪（严格审查）。

2. 看有无替代方案： 歧视性法规如果想合宪，必须证明 no reasonable alternative ➔ 考题中几乎总有替代方案（如限额、收费、交通控制等），因此几乎必死（违宪）。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state statute requires corporations located in the state to pay a use tax on equipment they purchased out-of-state for in-state use. The statute specifies that the use-tax rate is the same as the state's sales-tax rate for in-state equipment purchases. The statute also provides tax credits to corporations in the amount of the sales or use tax they paid on the same equipment in other states.
A construction company that builds homes in the state has refused to pay the state's use tax on equipment it purchased outside the state. The company has sued to challenge the state tax, arguing it is unconstitutional.
Is the state tax likely constitutional?

choices.A: No, because it discriminates against interstate commerce.
choices.B: No, because the commerce clause gives Congress the power to regulate interstate commerce.
choices.C: Yes, because it does not unduly burden interstate commerce.
choices.D: Yes, because the Tenth Amendment reserves to the states the power to construct their own tax system.

State taxation of interstate commerce
State taxes
  • Ad valorem property – tax on value of property in state
  • Sales – tax on sale of goods within state
  • Use – tax on goods purchased out-of-state but used within it
  • Doing business – tax on privilege to do business in state
↓
Tax affects interstate commerce

Complete Auto test
  • Substantial nexus between state & taxed person/activity
  • Fairly apportioned pursuant to rational formula
  • Not discriminatory against interstate commerce
  • Fairly related to state services/benefits
↓
Tax complies with dormant
commerce clause

The Tenth Amendment reserves to the states any power that the Constitution does not expressly grant to the federal government, including the power to construct a state tax system. But when exercising this power, states must comply with other constitutional provisions (Choice D). This includes the negative implication of the commerce clause (ie, dormant commerce clause), which prohibits states from unduly burdening interstate commerce.

A state tax on goods used in the state but purchased in another state (ie, use tax) affects interstate commerce. Therefore, to comply with the dormant commerce clause, the state tax must be:

  • applied to a person or activity that has a substantial nexus with the taxing state
  • fairly apportioned so that goods are not subject to multiple taxation in other states
  • not discriminatory against interstate commerce, which is established when the use-tax rate on goods purchased out-of-state is not higher than the sales-tax rate on goods purchased in-state and
  • fairly related to the benefits or services provided by the taxing state.

Here, there is a substantial nexus between the company and the state since the company builds homes there. The use tax is fairly apportioned because tax credits are provided for the sales or use tax that corporations paid on equipment in other states. The use tax is not discriminatory since it equals the state's sales tax for in-state equipment purchases (Choice A). It is also fairly related to the benefits provided by the state (eg, use of public roads). Therefore, the state tax does not unduly burden interstate commerce and is constitutional.

(Choice B) The commerce clause gives Congress the power to regulate interstate commerce. However, states may still tax goods within their borders if the tax satisfies the negative implication of this clause (as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

A state tax on goods purchased out-of-state for in-state use is valid if (1) the state has a substantial nexus with the taxed person or activity, (2) the tax is fairly apportioned, (3) the tax is nondiscriminatory, and (4) the tax is fairly related to benefits or services provided by the state.

📚 References
  • Complete Auto Transit, Inc. v. Brady, 430 U.S. 274, 279 (1977) (setting forth the four-factor test used to determine if a state tax violates the commerce clause).
  • Henneford v. Silas Mason Co., 300 U.S. 577, 584–85 (1937) (holding that a state's use tax on goods purchased out-of-state for in-state use is valid as long as the use-tax rate is not higher than the state's sales-tax rate).
  • 67B Am. Jur. 2d Sales and Use Taxes §§ 155–59 (explaining the four-factor test for determining whether a use tax violates the commerce clause).

一项州法律要求位于该州的公司，就其在州外购买并于州内使用的设备缴纳使用税。该法律规定，使用税的税率与该州对州内购买设备的销售税税率相同。该法律还规定，公司可获得税收抵免，抵免额度为其已在其他州就同一设备支付的销售税或使用税的金额。

一家在该州建造房屋的建筑公司，拒绝就其在州外购买的设备支付该州的使用税。该公司已提起诉讼以挑战该州的税收，主张其违宪。

该州的税收很可能合宪吗？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为它歧视了州际贸易。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为贸易条款授予国会监管州际贸易的权力。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为它没有对州际贸易构成不当负担。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为第十修正案将建立其自身税收体系的权力保留给了各州。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Federal-State Relations - State Taxation Of Commerce

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：州政府对在州外购买并带入州内使用的设备征收使用税（use tax），如果满足有实质联系、合理分摊、非歧视及合理关联服务四个要素，则不违反休眠商业条款，属于合宪税收。

三秒认题路径：

州外买设备带入本州 → 本州征收使用税（Use Tax） → 税率等同销售税且提供外州已纳税抵免（Tax Credit） → 满足 Complete Auto 四要素测试 → 未对跨州商业造成不当负担（No Undue Burden） → 合宪（Constitutional）

核心法律规则

州政府可以对跨州商业活动征税，但必须遵守 休眠商业条款（Dormant Commerce Clause），不得对跨州商业造成不当负担（unduly burden）。判断州税收是否合宪，须适用 Complete Auto 四要素测试（Complete Auto Test）：

  • 实质联系（Substantial Nexus）： 纳税人或征税活动与该州有显著的物理或经济联系（如在州内开展业务）。
  • 合理分摊（Fair Apportionment）： 税收必须合理分摊，避免对同一商品进行双重征税（通常通过提供 tax credits 抵免已向外州缴纳的税款来实现）。
  • 非歧视性（Nondiscriminatory）： 州税不得偏袒本地商业、歧视外州商业（例如，针对外地商品的 使用税（use tax） 税率不能高于本地商品的 销售税（sales tax））。
  • 合理关联服务（Fair Relation）： 征税必须与该州为纳税人提供的公共服务（如道路、警察和消防保护）合理相关。
核心判例： Complete Auto Transit, Inc. v. Brady (1977) —— 确立了州税收符合休眠商业条款的四要素测试法。本题中，使用税是对销售税的对等补偿（compensatory tax），且提供了外州纳税抵免，完全符合该四要素测试，因此合宪。

思维导图

1. 实质联系 (Substantial Nexus)
建商在州内建造房屋（builds homes），在该州有明显的实体运营。满足联系。
2. 合理分摊 (Fair Apportionment)
对在其他州已缴纳的销售/使用税提供等额抵免（tax credits），避免了双重征税。满足分摊。
3. 非歧视性 (Nondiscriminatory)
使用税率与州内销售税率完全相同（same rate），未对外州商品征收惩罚性高税。满足非歧视。
4. 合理关联服务 (Fair Relation)
建商利用州内公共公路运输设备并使用州内公共服务。满足关联。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：本案针对的是“外州购买的设备”，使用税可能构成对跨州商业的排他性歧视或双重征税。

但考试真正问的是：该州不仅将使用税率设为与销售税率完全一致，还提供了对等的外州纳税抵免（tax credits）。使用税（use tax）在法理上是为了平衡本地商品与外地商品税负的补偿性税收（compensatory tax），只要不加重外地商品负担且有抵免机制，就不构成歧视或双重征税。

司法考试看的是「实际税负效果是否平等且避免重复征税」，而不是「征税名目是否包含跨州交易」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

该州的使用税税率与销售税率一致，且提供外州已缴税款的 tax credits 抵免，未对跨州商业造成不当负担，完全符合 Complete Auto 测试。

❌ 事实误判 | 税率对等事实漏读

✕ A: 漏读税率一致且提供抵免的事实，该使用税作为 compensatory tax 并不构成歧视。

❌ 概念混淆 | 专属排他权限泛化

✕ B: 误认为国会商业条款权力排除了州的一切征税权，忽略了州在满足 Complete Auto 四要素时仍可征税。

❌ 法律适用 | 主权豁免优先度误判

✕ D: 错误套用 Tenth Amendment，州征税权并非不受限制，它依然受休眠商业条款的制约。

这题建议用什么方法？

补偿税审查法：看到州外商品被征收使用税，立即寻找“税率是否一致”与“是否有外州纳税抵免（tax credits）”两个关键事实。

考场速记

州税合宪性 Complete Auto 四要素速记：

跨州征税行不行，四项要素看端详：1. 实质联系（有物理/经济足迹）；2. 合理分摊（不双重征税，找 tax credits）；3. 非歧视性（本地外地一视同仁，使用税税率 ≤ 销售税率）；4. 关联服务（享受了州福利）。

记忆重点：使用税（use tax）通常是合宪的补偿性税收（compensatory tax），只要它不比本地销售税贵，并且给外州交过税的商品提供抵免，就不能选歧视或违宪！

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A man contracted with a moving company to ship household goods from the man's old home in State A to his new home in State B.
A federal statute provides that all liability of an interstate mover to a shipper for loss of or damage to the shipper's goods in transit is governed exclusively by the contract between them. The statute also requires the mover to offer a shipper at least two contracts with different levels of liability.
In full compliance with that federal statute, the moving company offered the man a choice between two shipping agreements that provided different levels of liability on the part of the moving company. The more expensive contract provided that the moving company was fully liable in case of loss or damage. The less expensive contract limited the moving company's liability in case of loss or damage to less than full value. The man voluntarily signed the less expensive contract, fixing the moving company's liability at less than the full value of the shipment.
The moving company's truck was involved in an accident in State B. The accident was entirely a product of the negligence of the moving company's driver. The man's household goods were destroyed. In accordance with the contract, the moving company reimbursed the man for less than the full value of the goods.
The man then brought suit against the moving company under the tort law of State B claiming that he was entitled to be reimbursed for the full value of the destroyed goods. The moving company filed a motion to dismiss.
In this suit, what action should the court take?

choices.A: Deny the motion to dismiss, because it is unconstitutional for a federal statute to authorize the moving company to contract out of any degree of liability for its own negligence.
choices.B: Deny the motion to dismiss, because the full faith and credit clause of the Constitution requires that state tort law be given effect.
choices.C: Dismiss the case, because the contractual relationship between the man and the moving company is governed by the obligation of contracts clause of the Constitution.
choices.D: Dismiss the case, because the federal statute governing liability of interstate carriers is the supreme law of the land and preempts state tort law.

questions.explanation:
Supremacy Clause
Supremacy Clause
US Constitution
Federal laws & treaties
State constitutions
State laws
Local laws

The federal government and states share many powers, so they often regulate the same subject matter. But under the supremacy clause, the U.S. Constitution, federal laws, and treaties are the supreme law of the land. As a result, they preempt (ie, supersede) conflicting state laws, state constitutions, and local laws.

Here, the man and the moving company entered into a contract that limited the moving company's liability. The man then sued under state tort law to hold the moving company fully liable. But a ruling in the man's favor would conflict with a federal statute requiring that such disputes be governed exclusively by their contract. And since the federal statute is the supreme law of the land and preempts state tort law, the court should dismiss the case.

(Choice A) The federal statute can authorize the moving company to contract out of any degree of liability for its own negligence. This is because the commerce clause gives Congress extensive power to regulate nearly any activity involving two or more states—including an interstate mover's degree of liability.

(Choice B) The Article IV full faith and credit clause requires states to respect public acts, records, and judicial proceedings of all other states. But it does not require courts to give effect to state laws that conflict with federal law (as seen here).

(Choice C) The contracts clause restricts the ability of state legislatures to impair existing contracts. But this clause does not apply to Congress or federal statutes that enforce existing contracts (as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

Under the supremacy clause, the U.S. Constitution, federal laws, and treaties preempt conflicting state laws, state constitutions, and local laws.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. VI, cl. 2 (supremacy clause).
  • Allis-Chalmers Corp. v. Lueck, 471 U.S. 202, 210–11 (1985) (holding that a federal law governing contracts preempts a conflicting state law on the same subject).
  • 16A Am. Jur. 2d Constitutional Law § 235 (2019) (discussing tests to determine if there is a conflict between federal and state law).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子与一家搬家公司签订合同，将其家居用品从其位于A州的旧家运往位于B州的新家。

一项联邦法规规定，州际搬运商对托运人货物在运输途中的灭失或损坏所承担的全部责任，完全由双方之间的合同管辖。该法规还要求搬运商向托运人提供至少两份具有不同责任水平的合同。

搬家公司完全遵守该联邦法规，向该男子提供了两份运输协议供其选择，这两份协议规定了搬家公司不同水平的责任。较昂贵的合同规定，在货物发生灭失或损坏的情况下，搬家公司承担全部责任。较便宜的合同则将搬家公司在货物发生灭失或损坏情况下的责任限制在低于货物全部价值的范围内。该男子自愿签署了较便宜的合同，将搬家公司的责任确定为低于货运物的全部价值。

搬家公司的卡车在B州发生了一起事故。该事故完全是由搬家公司司机的过失造成的。该男子的家居用品被毁。根据合同，搬家公司向该男子赔偿了低于货物全部价值的金额。

该男子随后依据B州的侵权法对搬家公司提起诉讼，声称他有权就其被毁货物的全部价值获得赔偿。搬家公司提交了驳回起诉的动议。

在此诉讼中，法院应采取何种行动？

zh-choices.A: 驳回该驳回起诉的动议，因为联邦法规授权搬家公司通过合同免除其因自身过失而产生的任何程度的责任是违宪的。
zh-choices.B: 驳回该驳回起诉的动议，因为宪法的“充分信任与尊重条款”(Full Faith and Credit Clause)要求州侵权法必须生效。
zh-choices.C: 驳回案件，因为该男子与搬家公司之间的合同关系受宪法“合同义务条款”(Contracts Clause)的管辖。
zh-choices.D: 驳回案件，因为管辖州际承运人责任的联邦法规是国家的最高法律，并优先于州侵权法。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Federal-State Relations - Miscellaneous

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：联邦立法在跨州商业领域对冲突州法具有预占力（Preemption），且限制契约自由的宪法条款（如合同条款）不适用于联邦立法。

三秒认题路径：

跨州货物运输 → 联邦法允许合同限制赔偿 vs 州侵权法要求全赔 → 联邦法优先（Supremacy Clause） → 预占州侵权法（Preemption） → 驳回起诉（Dismiss）

核心法律规则

1. 联邦预占（Federal Preemption）：根据宪法第六条的 至上条款（Supremacy Clause），符合宪法的联邦法律是国家的最高法律。若州法与联邦法发生冲突，或者联邦法已“预占”了该领域，则联邦法优于州法，冲突的州法无效。

2. 商业条款（Commerce Clause）：国会调节跨州商业活动的权力极宽，包括授权跨州承运人与寄件人签订限制过失赔偿责任的合同，该联邦立法完全合宪。

3. 合同条款（Contracts Clause / Obligation of Contracts Clause）：限制的是**州政府（States）**，禁止其立法损害既存合同义务；该条款**不限制联邦政府（Federal Government）**。

考场原则： 只要看到联邦法明文规定某事物“排他地受合同管辖”（governed exclusively by contract），而州法（侵权法或合同法）有不同规定，则该联邦法通过 Supremacy Clause 自动击溃州法，一切诉讼以联邦法和契约规定为准。

思维导图

第一步：国会是否有权制定此联邦立法？
YES: 跨州运输（Interstate Commerce）属于 商业条款（Commerce Clause） 的核心领域，国会立法绝对有效。
第二步：联邦立法与州侵权法是否存在冲突？
YES: 联邦法规定“限额合同排他决定赔偿”，而州侵权法支持“全额索赔”，两者直接冲突。
第三步：应如何解决此冲突？
适用原则： 根据 至上条款（Supremacy Clause），联邦法律自动 预占（Preempt） 州侵权法。
结论： 州法诉求被预占，法院必须予以驳回（Dismiss the case） ➔ 选 D
干扰项拦截（为什么不能阻止 Dismiss？）：
A 项：联邦立法授权免除自身过失责任违宪？ ➔ ❌ 错误。国会规制跨州商业极宽，不违宪。
B 项：完全信仰与信用条款（Full Faith & Credit）保护州法？ ➔ ❌ 错误。该条款管辖州际承认，不挑战联邦法律。
C 项：合同条款（Contracts Clause）管辖并认定违宪？ ➔ ❌ 错误。合同条款仅限制州，不能限制联邦法。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：运输公司因为自己的司机疏忽大意（negligence）毁了别人的全部家当，只赔一小部分太不公平了。宪法应该不允许合同免除由于自身过错造成的损失吧？

但考试真正问的是：在联邦法律明确授权责任限额合同时，州侵权法是否还有适用的空间？

司法考试看的是「联邦至上与预占规则（Supremacy & Preemption）」，而不是「个案中的物理损失或契约公平性」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

联邦法规制跨州承运人责任限额完全合宪，依 Supremacy Clause，该联邦法直接预占（preempt）州法，原告无权以州法索赔，法院应 Dismiss。

❌ 概念混淆 | 国会商业权边界误判

✕ A: 误认为国会无权允许过失责任限额，但跨州运输属于国会 Commerce Clause 核心权力，授权限责合同完全合法。

❌ 法律适用 | 完全信仰条款场景误判

✕ B: 错误引入 full faith and credit，该条款规范的是州与州之间的判决和法律承认，不能对抗联邦预占。

❌ 概念混淆 | 宪法约束主体张冠李戴

✕ C: 混淆了 obligation of contracts（合同条款）的约束主体，该限制只约束州，不能用来攻击联邦法律。

这题建议用什么方法？

联邦 vs. 州法直接冲突时，首选至上条款（Supremacy Clause）/ 预占（Preemption）路径；对限制条款，时刻注意“合同条款仅限制州”这一MBE高频陷阱。

考场速记

至上条款与合同条款双重判定秘籍：

  • 联邦与州法打架： 只要有有效的联邦法在场，且与州法/州诉求冲突，联邦法必然通过 preemption 胜出（排除州法）。
  • 合同条款（Contracts Clause）对象： 牢记 “States Only”。任何说“联邦法因为Contracts Clause而违宪”的选项，直接排除。
  • 跨州运输责任限制： 属于国会商业权领域，允许承运人通过合同免除/限制过失责任是完全合宪的，州法不能对此进行干预。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state statute provides that only corporations whose owners have been residents of the state for at least two years may obtain a retail license to sell liquor in the state. The stated purpose of the statute is to promote responsible alcohol sales and consumption through the local control of retail liquor stores.
A corporation's application for a liquor store license was denied because its owners had been state residents for less than two years. The corporation has sued to challenge the statute.
Is the state statute constitutional?

choices.A: No, because Congress has exclusive authority over interstate commerce.
choices.B: No, because it unduly burdens interstate commerce.
choices.C: Yes, because the issuance of licenses is a traditional government function.
choices.D: Yes, because the Twenty-first Amendment grants states authority to regulate alcohol.

questions.explanation:
Unconstitutional state alcohol regulations
Constitutional provision Example
Dormant commerce clause Permitting only in-state businesses to ship alcohol to in-state consumers
Free speech clause Banning advertisements featuring price of alcohol
Establishment clause Granting churches power to veto liquor license applications for businesses within 500-foot radius of church
Equal protection clause Permitting alcohol sales to females at age 18 but not to males until age 21

The Twenty-first Amendment grants states broad authority to regulate the use of alcohol within their own borders.* However, this authority is restricted by other constitutional provisions, including the dormant commerce clause (Choice D). The dormant commerce clause prohibits states from discriminating against or unduly burdening interstate commerce. A discriminatory state statute favors in-state over out-of-state interests. Such a statute is subject to strict scrutiny and is unconstitutional unless the state proves that:

  • the statute furthers a legitimate, non-economic state interest (eg, public health or safety) and
  • no reasonable alternative exists to further that interest.

Here, the state statute discriminates against interstate commerce by granting licenses to sell liquor only to corporations whose owners have been state residents for at least two years. Even if the statute furthers the state's legitimate, noneconomic interest in promoting responsible alcohol consumption, reasonable alternatives exist. For example, the state could limit the amount of alcohol that may be sold to individuals at one time. Therefore, the statute unduly burdens interstate commerce and is unconstitutional.

*The Twenty-first Amendment also repealed the Eighteenth Amendment's prohibition on the manufacture, transportation, and sale of alcohol in the United States.

(Choice A) Congress does have exclusive authority over interstate commerce. But if Congress has not enacted legislation in a particular area of interstate commerce, then the states are free to regulate that area so long as it does not discriminate against or unduly burden interstate commerce or regulate extraterritorial (ie, wholly out-of-state) activity.

(Choice C) The "traditional government function" exception allows states to favor government (not private) entities when those entities are performing a traditional government function (eg, waste disposal). Here, issuing licenses may be a traditional government function. But since the state is favoring in-state residents (as opposed to government entities), this exception does not apply.

📌 Educational Objective

The Twenty-first Amendment grants states broad authority to regulate alcohol within their borders. When doing so, states cannot violate the dormant commerce clause by discriminating against interstate commerce unless (1) the state statute furthers a legitimate, noneconomic state interest and (2) no reasonable alternative exists to do so.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. XXI (state's power to regulate alcohol).
  • Tenn. Wine & Spirits Retailers Ass'n v. Thomas, 139 S. Ct. 2449, 2476 (2019) (holding that a state statute requiring liquor store operators to be state residents for at least two years violates the dormant commerce clause).
  • 15A Am. Jur. 2d § 109 (2020) (explaining that the dormant commerce clause applies to state alcohol regulations).

一部州法律规定，只有其所有者已在该州居住至少两年的公司，才能获得在该州销售酒类的零售许可。该法规的既定目的是通过对零售酒类商店的本地控制，来促进负责任的酒类销售和消费。

一家公司的酒类商店许可申请被拒绝，因为其所有者在该州居住不到两年。该公司已提起诉讼，对该法规提出质疑。

该州法律是否合宪？

zh-choices.A: 不合宪，因为国会对州际贸易拥有专属管辖权。
zh-choices.B: 不合宪，因为它对州际贸易造成了不当负担。
zh-choices.C: 合宪，因为颁发许可是传统的政府职能。
zh-choices.D: 合宪，因为《Twenty-first Amendment》授予各州监管酒类的权力。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Federal-State Relations - Commerce

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：第21修正案赋予州规管酒类的权力，能否豁免休眠商业条款对跨州商业的歧视性限制。

三秒认题路径：

酒类执照居住限制 → 表面歧视外地人 → 触发休眠商业条款审查 → 第21修正案不豁免歧视 → 违宪

核心法律规则

1. 休眠商业条款（Dormant Commerce Clause, DCC）限制州政府制定歧视或过度负担跨州商业的法律。如果某项州法律在字面上歧视外地居民或商业（facial discrimination），则适用最严苛的严格审查。

2. 在严格审查下，该法律原则上违宪，除非州证明其促进了重大非经济利益，且没有其他合理的无歧视替代手段（no reasonable nondiscriminatory alternatives）。如果可以通过其他手段达到目的，该法律就不合理地负担了跨州商业（unduly burdens interstate commerce）。

3. 第21修正案（Twenty-first Amendment）赋予了州规管酒类的广泛权力，但该权力不是绝对的，**绝对不能凌驾于休眠商业条款之上**，州不能利用该修正案从事地方贸易保护。

核心判例： Granholm v. Heald & Tennessee Wine & Spirits Retailers Assn. v. Thomas —— 确立了第21修正案不能用来豁免对跨州商业的歧视，限制酒类执照所有人的居住年限属于典型的贸易保护主义，因违背DCC而违宪。

思维导图

第一关：州法律是否规管酒类？
YES: 激活第21修正案（21st Amendment）监管权，但仍须受制于休眠商业条款（DCC）。
第二关：该酒类法律是否歧视跨州商业？（本题：限制公司所有者须居住满2年）
YES: 构成表面歧视（facial discrimination），触发严格审查（strict scrutiny）。
第三关：州政府能否证明“没有合理的无歧视替代手段”？
NO: 存在替代手段（如限制单次销售量、加强店内培训等）。
❌ 严格审查未通过：构成不合理负担跨州商业（Undue Burden）
正确答案：州法律违宪（选 B）

考点陷阱

你可能会想：第21修正案既然允许各州规管酒类，那州政府规定谁能卖酒应该完全由州自己说了算，所以法律是合宪的（误选 D）。

但考试真正问的是：该限制是否通过对跨州商业施加不合理负担来实施贸易保护。第21修正案虽然赋予了各州监管酒类的“特权”，但极力禁止州政府实行“歧视外州居民的地方壁垒”。

核心区分：司法考试看的是「第21修正案的权力边界」，当它与休眠商业条款（DCC）冲突时，**禁止歧视**的原则依然至高无上。不要被“酒类监管传统权力”这一背景事实迷惑。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干限制两年居住属于对跨州商业的面上面向外地的歧视，且存在无歧视性替代手段，因此构成了对跨州商业的不合理负担而违宪。

❌ 概念混淆 | 权力界限误判

✕ A: 错误假设国会独占商业权，忽视了州在无冲突时的休眠规管空间 exclusive。

❌ 法律适用 | 例外场景误判

✕ C: 滥用例外，该例外仅适用于政府运营的非竞争性公用事业 traditional government function。

❌ 概念混淆 | 修正案效力泛化

✕ D: 误以为该修正案赋予州凌驾于休眠商业条款之上的绝对特权 Twenty-first Amendment。

这题建议用什么方法？

层级过滤法：只要看到酒类限制法案，先查有无跨州歧视，若有歧视直接套用休眠商业条款否定它。

考场速记

第21修正案与休眠商业条款（DCC）冲突时的核心速记：

看到州政府对酒类销售设置**「本地居民/本地持股时间」**等门槛限制，立刻联想休眠商业条款（DCC）严格审查。第21修正案（21st Amendment）虽然管酒，但打不过DCC的防歧视天平。州政府一旦实行地方保护主义，几乎必输。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
The childhood home of a former U.S. president is part of a national park located in a city. The National Park Service entered into a contract with an independent antique collector to acquire items owned by residents of the city during the former president's lifetime. According to the contract, the collector purchases items and then sells them to the Park Service at a price equal to the collector's cost plus a 10% commission. Purchases by antique collectors are ordinarily subject to the sales tax of the state in which the city is located.
The collector has filed suit in state court to enjoin collection of the tax on these purchases for the Park Service, claiming that the sales tax is unconstitutional as applied to them.
Should the state court issue the injunction?

choices.A: No, because as the purchaser of the antiques, the collector, rather than the federal government, is liable for the tax.
choices.B: No, because the suit is within the exclusive jurisdiction of the federal courts.
choices.C: Yes, because the federal government is contractually obligated to pay the amount of the sales tax when the government covers the collector's cost of the antiques.
choices.D: Yes, because under the supremacy clause, the federal program to acquire the antiques preempts the state sales tax on the purchase of these items.

questions.explanation:
Federal immunity from state tax/regulation
Who must comply with
state tax or regulation?
Direct tax/regulation
Federal government
(including agencies &
instrumentalities)
↓
Immune unless:
  • Congress expressly
    consents
Indirect tax/regulation
Affiliate of
federal government
(eg, employee, contractor)
↓
Must comply unless:
  • Congress grants immunity
    OR
  • Discrimination against or
    substantial interference
    with federal government

Under the Article VI supremacy clause, the federal government is generally immune from direct taxation by the states. This is because such taxes could hinder or destroy the operations of the federal government. But states can tax the federal government's affiliates, including persons or entities employed by or doing business with the federal government (eg, contractors—as seen here). This is true even if the cost of the tax is ultimately passed on to the federal government. As a result, an affiliate must pay these taxes unless:

  • Congress has granted the affiliate immunity
  • the tax discriminates against the federal government or the affiliate or
  • the tax substantially interferes with the affiliate's federal purpose or duties—eg, when a high tax burden makes it impossible for the affiliate to accomplish its federal functions.

Here, the independent antique collector (federal government affiliate) is responsible for paying the state sales tax when purchasing items to sell to the National Park Service. Although the federal government is contractually obligated to pay the amount of the sales tax when it covers the collector's cost, this is not a direct tax (Choice C). And since (1) Congress has not granted the collector immunity, (2) the tax is nondiscriminatory, and (3) there is no indication that it imposes a prohibitively high tax burden, the state should not be enjoined from collecting this tax.

(Choice B) Federal courts do not have exclusive jurisdiction over suits arising under federal law (as seen here) since state courts also have jurisdiction over such suits.

(Choice D) The supremacy clause also allows federal law to preempt conflicting state law. But there is no direct conflict here since the antique collector can pay the sales tax without violating federal law. And there is no indirect conflict since the collector can still acquire antiques to accomplish the federal program's purpose.

📌 Educational Objective

States can tax federal government affiliates (eg, employees) unless (1) Congress granted the affiliate immunity, (2) the tax is discriminatory, or (3) the tax substantially interferes with the affiliate's federal purpose or duties.

📚 References
  • Alabama v. King & Boozer, 314 U.S. 1, 8–9 (1941) (holding that a state can tax a federal contractor even if the tax is passed on to the federal government).
questions.zh-question:
一位美国前总统的童年故居是位于某市的国家公园的一部分。National Park Service与一名独立的古董收藏家签订合同，以收购该市居民在前总统有生之年拥有的物品。根据合同，该收藏家购买物品，然后以其成本价加上10%佣金的价格出售给Park Service。古董收藏家的购买行为通常需要缴纳该市所在州的销售税。

该收藏家已向州法院提起诉讼，请求禁止对这些为Park Service进行的采购征收税款，声称对他们适用销售税是违宪的。

州法院是否应发出此项禁令？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为作为古董的购买者，收藏家而非联邦政府，应对该税款承担责任。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为该诉讼属于联邦法院的专属管辖权范围。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为当联邦政府承担收藏家的古董成本时，其在合同上有义务支付销售税的金额。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为根据至高条款 (supremacy clause)，收购古董的联邦计划优先于州对这些物品购买行为征收的销售税。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Federal-State Relations - State immunity

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：联邦免税权（Federal Immunity）仅直接豁免联邦实体本身的纳税义务，不适用于与联邦交易的独立承包商（Independent Contractor），即使税款最终由联邦政府报销（即经济负担转嫁）。

三秒认题路径：

古董商买古董转卖联邦 → 州对古董商课税 → 古董商是纳税主体（非联邦） → 联邦合同报销仅属经济转嫁 → 州税合宪，不予禁令（选 A）

核心法律规则

根据宪法第六条的 最高条款（Supremacy Clause），各州在未经国会明示同意前，禁止直接对联邦政府及其机构或派出工具进行课税（即 联邦免税权 Federal Immunity）。

但是，此免税特权并不保护与联邦做生意的关联方或独立承包商。即便税款成本最终由联邦承担，承包商也必须缴纳普通的、不具歧视性的州销售税，除非：

  • 国会已明文授予该关联方免税地位；或者
  • 该州税对联邦政府或其关联方构成了差别歧视；或者
  • 该税收实质性干扰了联邦公务的正常履行。
核心判例： United States v. New Mexico (1982) —— 确立了除非国会明文豁免，否则各州可对与联邦政府订立合同的独立承包商征收销售税和使用税，即使税收负担最终转嫁至联邦。

思维导图

州税务部门 State Tax Authority
➔ 课征销售税
法律纳税义务 (Legal Incidence)
古董商 (独立承包商) Independent Contractor ⚠️ 法律纳税主体
➔ 转嫁税收与成本
Economic Burden
国家公园管理局 Federal NPS 合同买单人 (非直接纳税人)

考点陷阱

你可能会想：联邦国家公园管理局在合同中承诺全额报销古董商所付的税款，这说明钱其实是联邦政府出的，那这税岂不是变相征在了联邦头上？

但考试真正问的是：法律上的直接纳税义务人（Legal Incidence）究竟是谁？ 司法考试只看法律由谁向州缴税，不看幕后谁在合同中为这笔税款买单。由于购买者是独立的古董商（承包商），税也是他付的，因此属于合宪的间接税。

司法考试看的是「法律纳税主体是谁」，而不是「税款最终由谁报销」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

古董商属于独立承包商，购买古董时的 purchaser 且法定纳税人是他本人而非联邦政府，故州税合宪，不应签发禁令。

❌ 概念混淆 | 专属管辖误判

✕ B: 误认为涉及联邦宪法和政府免税权的案件属于联邦法院的 exclusive jurisdiction，实际上州法院同样有权管辖。

❌ 法律适用 | 经济负担与法律义务混淆

✕ C: 误以为联邦在合同中报销税款的 contractually obligated 义务能将该税转化为针对联邦的直接税。

❌ 事实误判 | 联邦预占权滥用

✕ D: 错误援引 preempts（预占），联邦收购总统旧居文物的计划并未与州征收普通销售税产生任何冲突。

这题建议用什么方法？

主体区分法：看到联邦合同工（contractor）被征州税，直接确认他是法律纳税人，瞬间排除主张免税的 Yes 选项。

考场速记

联邦免税权（Federal Tax Immunity）判定口诀：

“直接税联邦，绝对不可以；间接税关联，三无就合法。”

核心提要：如果州直接向联邦实体或财产征税，绝对违宪。如果州向联邦的关联方（如承包商/雇员）征税，只要满足以下“三无”条件即为合宪：

  • 无立法特权：国会未通过明文立法给予其免税地位。
  • 无任何歧视：属于普适性税种，未针对联邦或其关联方差别对待。
  • 无实质干涉：未严重阻碍或使关联方无法履行联邦职能（合同报销税款绝不构成干涉）。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Small retailers located in a state are concerned about the loss of business to certain large retailers located nearby in bordering states. In an effort to deal with this concern, the state legislature enacted a statute requiring all manufacturers and wholesalers that sell goods to retailers in the state to do so at prices that are no higher than the lowest prices at which they sell them to retailers in any of the bordering states.
Several manufacturers and wholesalers that are located in bordering states and that sell their goods to retailers in the state bring an action in federal court to challenge the constitutionality of this statute.
Which of the following arguments offered by these plaintiffs is likely to be most persuasive in light of applicable precedent?

choices.A: The state statute denies them the equal protection of the laws.
choices.B: The state statute deprives them of a privilege or immunity of national citizenship.
choices.C: The state statute deprives them of their property or liberty without due process of law.
choices.D: The state statute imposes an unreasonable burden on interstate commerce.

The commerce clause gives Congress the power to regulate interstate commerce. The negative implication of this clause (i.e., the dormant commerce clause) is that states cannot discriminate against or otherwise unduly burden interstate commerce. As a result, state regulations that purposefully or deliberately regulate out-of-state conduct (i.e., extraterritorial regulations) are unconstitutional—even if the regulated conduct affects commerce within the state.

Here, the state statute is an extraterritorial regulation since it deliberately regulates out-of-state conduct. That is because the statute requires all manufacturers and wholesalers selling goods in the state to do so at prices that are no higher than the lowest prices they charge retailers in bordering states. This requires out-of-state commerce to be conducted in accordance with the state statute. Therefore, the most persuasive argument that the statute is unconstitutional is that it imposes an unreasonable burden on interstate commerce.

(Choice A) State laws that substantially impact a fundamental right or intentionally discriminate against a protected class almost always violate the Fourteenth Amendment equal protection clause. But there is no fundamental right to sell goods, and out-of-state businesses are not a protected class. As a result, the state statute does not deny the plaintiffs the equal protection of the laws.

(Choice B) The Fourteenth Amendment privileges or immunities clause* bars states from depriving individuals of the very limited rights of national citizenship—which do not include the right to sell goods.

*The privileges or immunities clause is almost always an incorrect answer choice on the MBE.

(Choice C) Under the Fourteenth Amendment due process clause, state laws cannot deprive an individual of life, liberty, or property without adequate justification. Laws that substantially impact a fundamental right are generally unjustified under strict scrutiny. But since no fundamental right is implicated here, the state statute is likely justified under rational basis scrutiny.

📌 Educational Objective

The dormant commerce clause prohibits states from enacting regulations that purposefully or deliberately regulate out-of-state conduct—e.g., by requiring out-of-state commerce to be conducted in accordance with a state statute.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. I, § 8, cl. 3 (commerce clause).
  • Healy v. Beer Inst., Inc., 491 U.S. 324, 336–39 (1989) (holding that price-affirmation statutes violate the dormant commerce clause since they regulate commerce in other states).
  • Nat'l Pork Producers Council v. Ross, 143 S. Ct. 1142, 1155–57 (2023) (explaining that states may not purposefully or deliberately regulate conduct that occurs wholly beyond their borders).

几家位于邻近州份并向该州零售商销售商品的制造商和批发商，向联邦法院提起诉讼，挑战该法规的合宪性。

根据适用的判例，这些原告提出的以下哪项论点最有可能具有说服力？

zh-choices.A: 该州法规剥夺了他们受法律平等保护的权利。
zh-choices.B: 该州法规剥夺了他们作为国家公民的特权或豁免权。
zh-choices.C: 该州法规未经正当法律程序剥夺了他们的财产或自由。
zh-choices.D: 该州法规对州际贸易施加了不合理的负担。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Federal-State Relations - The Dormant Commerce Clause

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：州法要求在本州销售的批发商/制造商，定价不得高于其在邻州零售商的最低价——这种域外规制（extraterritorial regulation）是否违反休眠商业条款（dormant commerce clause）。

价格确认法 邻州最低价 州际商业负担 Healy
三秒认题路径：

州法管定价 → 参照邻州价格 → 控制外州行为 → 域外规制 → 选 D

核心法律规则

商业条款（commerce clause）授权国会规制州际商业；其否定含义即休眠商业条款（dormant commerce clause）——考场意思：州不能歧视或unduly burden州际商业。

州法若故意规制州外行为（purposefully regulate out-of-state conduct），即属域外规制（extraterritorial regulation）——考场意思：哪怕交易发生在本州，只要法律实质上要外州商家按本州规则在邻州定价，就违宪。本题正是价格确认法（price-affirmation statute）：表面管本州销售，实则把手伸进邻州定价。

因此最有力的挑战理由是：该法对州际商业施加不合理负担（unreasonable burden on interstate commerce）——所以选 D，不是选第十四修正案那三条。

核心判例：Healy v. Beer Inst., Inc.（1989）——价格确认法因规制他州商业而违反休眠商业条款；Nat'l Pork Producers Council v. Ross（2023）——州不得故意规制完全发生在州境外的行为。

思维导图

州法要求：卖给本州零售商的价格 ≤ 邻州零售商最低价？
是 →表面管本州交易，实则控制外州定价行为
下一步 →
是否域外规制（extraterritorial regulation）？
是 →州故意把规则强加到外州商业上
✕ 即使影响本州商业，域外规制仍违宪（Healy 先例）
排除 →
第十四修正案三条路径能赢吗？
A 平等保护 →无基本权利、外州企业非受保护群体 → 否
B 特权或豁免 →卖货权不在国家公民权之列 → 否
C 正当程序 →仅rational basis审查，州易过关 → 否
结论 → D：对州际商业施加不合理负担 ✓

考点陷阱

你可能会想：这是州内定价规则，只保护本州小零售商，用equal protection或due process挑战更「宪法」。

但考试真正问的是：这条法律的手有没有伸到邻州定价——伸了就是域外规制，休眠商业条款直接否决，不必绕第十四修正案。

司法考试看的是「法律规制的地理边界」，而不是「本州小企业有没有吃亏」。小零售商丢生意是背景故事，不改变宪法分析路径。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干要求定价参照邻州最低价，属域外规制，直接违反休眠商业条款（dormant commerce clause）。

❌ 概念混淆 | 审查标准误判

✕ A: 卖货非基本权利，外州企业非受保护群体，equal protection 过不了。

❌ 法律适用 | 条款几乎总错

✕ B: 第十四修正案privileges or immunities极少正确，卖货权不在其列。

❌ 事实误判 | 基本权利缺失

✕ C: 无基本权利涉入，due process 只走理性基础，州法易过关。

这题建议用什么方法？

先问法律规制的是本州还是外州行为；伸到外州 → 休眠商业条款，直接排除 A/B/C。

考场速记

域外规制速记：看到州法定价/销售条件参照邻州价格或行为 → 联想 Healy → 休眠商业条款 → 选「不合理负担州际商业」。

第十四修正案排雷：商业规制题里，特权或豁免条款（privileges or immunities clause）几乎永远是干扰项；无基本权利时，正当程序（due process）与平等保护（equal protection）也打不过休眠商业条款。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
After several well-publicized deaths caused by fires in products made from highly flammable fabrics, State A enacted a statute prohibiting "the manufacture or assembly of any product in this state which contains any fabric that has not been tested and approved for flame retardancy by a specific privately owned and operated testing company located in State A."
For many years, a fabric mill located in State A has had its fabric tested for flame retardancy by a privately owned and operated testing company located in State B. This testing company is a reliable organization that uses a process for testing and approving fabrics for flame retardancy identical in all respects to that used by the State A testing company.
Because the fabric mill wishes to continue to have its fabric tested solely by the State B testing company, the fabric mill files an action in a State A court challenging the constitutionality of the State A statute as applied to its circumstances.
In this suit, should the court hold the statute to be constitutional?

choices.A: No, because it denies the fabric mill the equal protection of the laws.
choices.B: No, because it imposes an unreasonable burden on interstate commerce.
choices.C: Yes, because it is a legitimate means of protecting the safety of the public.
choices.D: Yes, because it is reasonably related to the protection of the reputation of the fabric industry located in State A.

questions.explanation:
Dormant commerce clause (state regulation of interstate commerce)
Type of regulation Examples Standard
Discriminatory
(favors in-state interests)		 • Taxing out-of-state products more heavily
• Requiring use of in-state products/services 		Unconstitutional unless:
• furthers legitimate state interest and
• no reasonable alternative
Nondiscriminatory
(otherwise burdensome)		 • Prohibiting all commercial vehicles on state highways
• Overly strict requirements for all commercial shipments 		Unconstitutional if:
• burden clearly exceeds local benefits

The states' power to regulate interstate commerce is restricted by the dormant commerce clause, which prohibits states from discriminating against or otherwise unduly burdening interstate commerce.

Discrimination against interstate commerce—ie, favoring in-state over out-of-state economic interests—is invalid unless:

• it furthers a legitimate, noneconomic state interest (eg, public health and safety) and

• no reasonable alternative exists.

Here, the State A statute discriminates against interstate commerce since it requires that an in-state company test flame retardancy. The statute promotes the state's legitimate, noneconomic interest in ensuring safety. But reasonable alternatives are available—eg, allowing any reliable organization, including the State B company, to conduct these tests. Therefore, the statute is unconstitutional as applied to these circumstances because it unreasonably burdens interstate commerce (Choice C).

(Choice A) State laws that substantially impact a fundamental right or intentionally discriminate against a protected class almost always violate the Fourteenth Amendment equal protection clause. But since no fundamental right is implicated and businesses are not a protected class, the statute likely does not deny the fabric mill the equal protection of the laws.

(Choice D) A state law that discriminates against interstate commerce must further a legitimate, noneconomic state interest and no reasonable alternatives can exist. Therefore, the fact that the statute is reasonably related to State A's economic interest in protecting the reputation of State A's fabric industry does not justify the statute.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the dormant commerce clause, states cannot discriminate against interstate commerce unless (1) the discrimination furthers a legitimate, noneconomic state interest and (2) no reasonable alternative exists.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. I, § 8, cl. 3 (commerce clause).
  • Maine v. Taylor, 477 U.S. 131, 138 (1986) (explaining that state discrimination against interstate commerce is invalid unless it furthers a legitimate, noneconomic state interest and no reasonable alternatives exist).
questions.zh-question:
在数起因高度易燃织物制成的产品起火而导致的死亡事件被广泛报道后，A州颁布了一项法规，禁止“在本州制造或组装任何含有未经A州某特定私营检测公司进行阻燃性测试和批准的织物的任何产品”。

多年来，位于A州的一家纺织厂一直将其织物交由位于B州的一家私营检测公司进行阻燃性测试。该检测公司是一个可靠的组织，其使用的织物阻燃性测试和批准程序在所有方面都与A州检测公司所使用的程序相同。

由于该纺织厂希望继续仅由B州的检测公司对其织物进行测试，该纺织厂在A州法院提起诉讼，就A州法规在其情况下的适用，对其合宪性提出质询。

在此诉讼中，法院是否应裁定该法规合宪？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为它剥夺了该纺织厂受法律平等保护的权利。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为它对州际贸易施加了不合理的负担。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为它是保护公众安全的一种合法手段。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为它与保护A州纺织业的声誉有合理关联。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Federal-State Relations - The Dormant Commerce Clause

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：A 州强制布料必须经本州指定私营检测公司认证，这种歧视州际商业（discrimination against interstate commerce）的法规，能否通过休眠商业条款（dormant commerce clause）审查。

三秒认题路径：

强制本州检测 → 歧视州外服务 → 查两要件 → 有合理替代 → 违宪 → 选 B

核心法律规则

州法若歧视州际商业（discriminatory）——考场意思：只认本州产品/服务、把州外竞争者挡在外面——原则上违宪；唯一例外须同时满足两要件：（1）推进正当非经济州利益；（2）不存在合理替代方案。

若法规非歧视但负担过重（nondiscriminatory but burdensome）——考场意思：对州内外一视同仁地加规——则看负担是否明显超过本地收益；本题不用走这条路，因为法规已明显偏袒本州检测公司。

本题虽有公共安全（public health and safety）这一正当利益，但 B 州检测公司流程完全相同且可靠——州完全可以让任何可靠机构检测——所以第二要件失败，法规合宪性不成立。

核心判例：Maine v. Taylor, 477 U.S. 131 (1986) — 歧视州际商业的州法规，须证明推进正当非经济利益且别无合理替代；本案 B 州公司即为合理替代，例外不成立。

思维导图

法规是否歧视州际商业？
只许本州指定私营公司检测 = 偏袒本州、排斥州外
是 →适用歧视法规严格审查（Maine v. Taylor 两要件）
要件 1：正当非经济州利益？
✓ 防火安全 = 正当非经济利益
要件 2：无合理替代方案？
✗ B 州公司流程完全相同、同样可靠 → 合理替代存在 → 例外不成立
结论： 违宪 → 对州际商业施加不合理负担 → 选 B（No）
若否 →改查负担是否明显超过收益（本题不走此路）

考点陷阱

你可能会想：法规目的是防止易燃布料致死，protecting safety 这么重要，法院应该会判合宪（选 C 或 D）。

但考试真正问的是：州有没有用「最少歧视」的方式达到安全目的。安全利益只过第一关；第二关问「能不能让州外同样可靠的机构检测」——能，所以歧视性规定仍违宪。

另一陷阱：看到企业被区别对待就想选平等保护（equal protection）——但企业不是受保护阶层，也没有基本权利被触及，A 不是正确路径。

还有陷阱：把「保护本州布料业声誉」当成正当理由——这是经济利益（economic interest），不是非经济利益，不能为歧视州际商业背书。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 只认本州指定检测公司属歧视州际商业，B 州替代方案同样可靠，对州外商业施加不合理负担，法规违宪。

❌ 概念混淆 | 错用平等保护

✕ A: 企业非受保护阶层，equal protection 不是本题考点。

❌ 法律适用 | 只看利益不看替代

✕ C: 安全利益过第一关，但 reasonable alternative 存在，仍违宪。

❌ 事实误判 | 经济利益当正当理由

✕ D: 保护本州产业声誉是economic interest，不能justify歧视。

这题建议用什么方法？

先判歧视性与否，歧视法则走 Maine 两要件，第二要件「合理替代」往往是决胜关。

考场速记

歧视性州法规口诀：「安全不够，还得没替代」——正当非经济利益 + 无合理替代，两关都过才合宪。

快速分类：只认本州产品/服务 → 歧视 → 严格两要件；一视同仁加负担 → 非歧视 → 看负担是否明显超过收益。

排除捷径：企业 ≠ 平等保护；保护本地产业声誉 = 经济利益，救不了歧视性法规。

question_analysis.skill_tested: Applying the Dormant Commerce Clause test

reason.en: Identifies the source of the government action being challenged.
reason.zh: 识别出被挑战的政府行为来源。

keywords.text: testing company located in State A

reason.en: Indicates favoritism towards in-state economic interests, showing discrimination.
reason.zh: 表明对州内经济利益的偏袒，构成歧视。

reason.en: Shows the restriction affects commerce involving an out-of-state entity.
reason.zh: 显示该限制影响了涉及州外实体的商业活动。

reason.en: Shows that the out-of-state company is just as safe, highlighting that less discriminatory alternatives exist.
reason.zh: 表明州外公司同样安全，突显存在歧视性更小的替代方案。

reason.en: Defines the legal nature of the plaintiff's lawsuit.
reason.zh: 界定了原告起诉的法律性质。

reason.en: Incorrectly applies equal protection standard instead of the Dormant Commerce Clause.
reason.zh: 错误地应用了平等保护标准，而非休眠商业条款。

reason.en: Correctly identifies the core standard for invalidating discriminatory state laws under the Dormant Commerce Clause.
reason.zh: 正确指出了休眠商业条款下宣布歧视性州法无效的核心标准。

C.text: protecting the safety of the public

reason.en: Focuses on the state's safety purpose while overlooking the availability of non-discriminatory alternatives.
reason.zh: 仅关注州的安全性目的，而忽略了存在非歧视性替代方案这一事实。

D.text: protection of the reputation of the fabric industry located in State A

reason.en: Tries to justify state discrimination using local economic protectionism, which is constitutionally impermissible.
reason.zh: 试图使用地方经济保护主义来为州歧视辩护，这在宪法上是不允许的。

highlights.text: prohibiting "the manufacture or assembly of any product in this state which contains any fabric that has not been tested and approved for flame retardancy by a specific privately owned and operated testing company located in State A."

reason.en: The statute on its face requires testing by an in-state company, which discriminates against out-of-state competitors.
reason.zh: 该法规在表面上要求由州内公司进行测试，从而歧视了州外竞争对手。

highlights.text: This testing company is a reliable organization that uses a process for testing and approving fabrics for flame retardancy identical in all respects to that used by the State A testing company.

reason.en: Demonstrates that the out-of-state testing is identical, showing that State A's safety goals could be met without discriminating.
reason.zh: 证明了州外测试是相同的，表明州法无需通过歧视性手段也可实现其安全目标。

highlights.text: challenging the constitutionality of the State A statute as applied to its circumstances

label.zh: 针对具体情况适用的休眠商业条款挑战

reason.en: Defines the scope of the constitutional challenge brought by the fabric mill.
reason.zh: 界定了该布料厂提出的宪法挑战的范围。
